When we hearing this criminal reference, then it is observed that learned Second Sessions Judge/Special Judge, POCSO Act, Itarsi District Narmadapuram (MP) while deciding the POCSO Sessions Case No.71/2022 reserved the case for judgment on 13/02/2023.

sentences.text: It delivered judgment of conviction under Sections 363, 376(A)(B), 376(2)(F) & 302 of IPC and Section 5(M)/5(N)/6 of POCSO Act on 21/02/2023 and on the same date passed the sentence.

Sub-section (2) of Section 235 of Cr.P.C. provides that if the accused is convicted, the judge shall,
unless he proceeds in accordance with the provisions of Section 360, hear the accused on the question of sentence and then pass sentence on him according to law.

Shri Aditya Adhikari - Senior Advocate assisted by Shri Satish Chand Chaturvedi - Advocate and Shri Atul Anand Awasthi, Senior Advocate assisted by Shri Satish Chand Chaturvedi - Advocate submits that adherence to Section 235(2) of Cr.P.C. is mandatory and there appears to be breach of this provision.

2 CRRFC-2-2023 Shri Adhikari, Senior Advocate placing reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Allauddin Mian and others, Sharif Mian and another vs. State of Bihar, (1989) 3 SCC 5 , to submits that in Para-10 of this judgment Hon'ble Supreme Court has taken note of the provisions contained in sub-section (2) of Section 235 of the Cr.P.C. and has held as under "The requirement of hearing, the accused in intended to satisfy the rule of natural justice

sentences.text: found guilty, be asked if he has anything to say or any evidence to tender on the question of sentence.
This is all the more necessary since the courts are generally required to make the choice from a wide range of discretion in the matter of sentencing.
To assist the court in determining the correct sentence to be imposed the legislature introduced sub-section(2) to Section 235.

The said provision therefore satisfies a dual purpose; it satisfied the rule of natural justice by according to the accused an opportunity of being heard on the question of sentence and at the same time held the court to choose the sentence to be awarded.

Since the provision is intended to give the accused an opportunity to place before the court all the relevant material having a bearing on the question of sentence there can be no doubt that the provision is salutary and must be strictly followed.
It is clearly mandatory and should not be treated as a mere formality."
There are two options available for us.

One to remand the matter to the learned trial Judge for hearing afresh on sentence or as agreed between the parties, call for the report of the Social Welfare Officer of the State, Station at Betul in regard to the family background and past conduct of the appellant so also another report from the Jail where he is lodged, about his conduct which may become a mitigating circumstances to decide the finality of sentence.
Let report be called for.
Shri Nitin Gupta, Government Advocate undertakes to call for both the reports within one week.
List the matter in the week commencing 18/08/2025.
Certified copy today.
(VIVEK AGARWAL)
